items.title: Paris Agreement targets
items.claim: The Paris Agreement (2015) commits parties to holding warming below 2 C and pursuing efforts to limit it to what?
items.reveal:
Article 2 of the Paris Agreement specifies 'well below 2 C' and 'pursuing efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5 C'. IPCC's 2018 SR15 report assessed the 1.5 C pathway in detail.

In 2023 the global mean temperature anomaly briefly exceeded 1.5 C above pre-industrial.
items.why: Climate policy numbers carry technical meaning beyond their headline use.

items.title: IPCC AR6 on attribution
items.claim: IPCC AR6 Working Group I (2021) concluded what about the cause of observed warming since around 1850?

options.text: It is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land

items.reveal:
The AR6 WGI Summary for Policymakers (2021) used 'unequivocal' for the first time in IPCC headline statements.

The assessment also tightened estimates of climate sensitivity to a likely range of 2.5-4 C per CO2 doubling.
items.why: IPCC's calibrated language tracks evolving confidence as evidence accumulates.

items.title: Methane's GWP comparison
items.claim: Methane is a more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 over short timescales. Approximately how does its 100-year global warming potential compare?

options.text: Around 28-30 times CO2 over 100 years (IPCC AR6)

items.reveal_title: About 28-30x over 100 years; closer to 80x over 20 years
items.reveal:
IPCC AR6 reports GWP-100 of around 27-30 for fossil and biogenic methane. Methane's atmospheric lifetime is about 12 years, making it a strong near-term lever.

The Global Methane Pledge (2021) targets a 30% cut by 2030.
items.why: Choice of GWP averaging window shapes how big methane appears to be as a problem.
